decisions.decision: The methodology has five layers that form a loop (Purpose, Knowledge, Operations, Execution, Evidence) and two that cut across them (Governance, Interface). Knowledge is SAD; Operations is MAD.

The Everything Ecosystem is a schema, described as the AI-Native OS for Builders. An instance is one person's workspace, declared by a workspace.json naming the schema version it follows. The schema does not depend on any instance.

A workspace is made of spheres. Each person has one personal sphere as the root, holding their values. Every other sphere (household, employer, venture, client, community, learning) has a parent; clients exist only inside the venture that serves them. Every sphere has the same layers at the depth it needs, records its purpose as weights over the root's values, and links one way: no sphere reads the root.
decisions.why: Named after sphere sovereignty (each sphere governs itself; borders are kept). "Domain" was rejected because it already means a subject area in domain design and in MAD.

decisions.decision: Venture is the one kind for anything a person undertakes. Hobby, venture and company are stages of it: a hobby is done for its own sake, a venture is an undertaking with risk not yet formed into a company, and a company is formalized with a legal form (llc, s-corp, c-corp, sole-prop, partnership, nonprofit). A venture changes stage without moving folders. Grouping folders such as ventures/companies/ are for browsing only; sphere.json is the truth.
Docs as code: the method, design docs, schemas, skills and templates live in this repo. An instance keeps its own notes, philosophy and decisions in its own spheres.

A handoff includes a self-proof step (the agent exercises its change for real), allows 3 attempts and a 2-hour run cap before escalating, and ends with a one-line lesson when something failed for a reason that could recur.

Each layer lists its tools in <layer>/tooling/integrations.json. Choosing tools is opt-in: when someone wants help, the agent asks situation questions from the layer's principles and examples, and scores with Jev plus a reasoning model; people who name their tools just have them recorded.

The sphere is the unit of an instance, and "sphere" is the name used in files and in conversation. Each sphere keeps a sphere.json (machine fields) beside a human-readable profile (narrative, pillars, changelog), named by sphere.json's profile field. Products and systems inside a venture are not spheres; product cards describe them.
decisions.why: Sphere reads plainly to a person and avoids "domain", which already means a subject area in domain design and in MAD.

decisions.decision: Personal life is out of scope. A sphere is a venture or a client inside a venture; there is no personal root, and household, employer, community and learning kinds are dropped, with values and purpose weights. Top-level spheres are ventures. Personal knowledge management will be a separate system, built on its own, that can later read from or share with an instance through links.
decisions.why: Keeps the schema about what a builder builds. The personal system has different needs (values, axiology, life areas) and is better designed on its own, then joined.

decisions.decision: The company template (governance/company-template/) stays, as the venture template. Its three pillars (product, brand, business) are scaffolded into every venture at every stage, because even a venture that is not a legal entity has a product, a brand and a business side. Governance (roles and decision rights) still starts only at the company stage.

The venture is the unit of an instance, replacing the sphere. A venture is anything a builder undertakes, from a hobby to a company, and ventures can hold ventures. Each keeps a venture.json beside its venture profile (the readable companion, replacing the entity profile). Products are cards in products/, holding their own market, job, technology, offering and business model; venture.json keeps only what is true of the whole venture (phase, ambition, form, industry, core product). Clients are records in clients/ inside the venture that serves them, no longer units. The company template is renamed the venture template.
decisions.why: "A venture is a venture": the plain word needs no new noun. Product-level fields were checked against Product Anatomy, where markets, jobs and business models already vary by product and phase.

decisions.decision: Phase replaces stage. A venture's phases are Discovery, Validation, Beachhead, Scale and Platform, each with a gate for leaving it: problem-solution fit, product-market fit (retention holds), repeatability, market leadership with healthy margins, and others building on it. Formalization is form.legal_form; intent is ambition (hobby, survival, lifestyle, managed growth, aggressive growth). The core product is required once a venture leaves Discovery. Starting layers come from the phase; governance switches on when the venture is formalized.
decisions.why: Stage and phase meant the same thing. Names follow Blank (Discovery, Validation) and Moore (Beachhead, Scale); retention and repeatability, from a six-phase model the founder shared, became gates so the Succession Matrix keeps its weights. Horizon became Platform because McKinsey's horizons are concurrent, not sequential.

decisions.decision: Nouns that meant two things are split. Layer means only the system's seven layers; MAD's four become tiers. A product's place in the portfolio is its portfolio role; a bare role is a person's or agent's job. Wedge keeps its business meaning, a portfolio role (the narrow product used to enter a market), and is not a phase. The proposed for-profit/nonprofit axis is dropped: legal form carries it, with benefit-corp added.
decisions.why: Founder rejected renaming wedge to on-ramp: in business those are different things.

decisions.decision: The system is highly opinionated, with references at every layer. Standards first: a noun uses an established term with its standard meaning and is coined only when none exists. docs/ontology.json is canonical for nouns (docs/ontology.md is generated from it); schema/check-nouns.mjs fails when a retired noun reappears. Each layer records the sources behind its defaults, and the alternatives weighed, in <layer>/references/references.json with title, authors, year, summary, a URL when one exists and a stance; the find-reference skill fills and re-checks them. The genus of the whole (operating system or operating model) stays open until the first venture runs end to end; files say "the system".
decisions.why: A loosely opinionated system is hard to build; references keep the defaults discoverable. URLs rot, so titles are always recorded too.

decisions.decision: Kits have a scope. A product card may name its scope (the whole system, one layer, or one tier of the operations layer) and the kits it is part of (part_of); a part can still be its own product. The Everything Ecosystem's own schema and method skills are one offering, the system kit; some skills, such as the five-step algorithm skill, are also products by themselves.
decisions.why: Found by the first venture run: skills and schema tied as flagship, and the owner confirmed they are one offering while some skills stand alone and some kits serve one layer or tier.

decisions.decision: The interface layer holds interfaces only: tools through which a person, with agents, works across at least four of the six other layers in one session. Agent harnesses (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) are the default kind and the operator console is a custom one. A tool that serves one or two layers is an integration of those layers (Obsidian under knowledge), checked by schema/check-integrations.mjs. Three AI levels, recorded as a product's ai field: AI feature (the product works without the model), AI harness (the product is the software around a model; a chatbot), agent harness (an AI harness where the model directs its own steps and tool use toward a goal). Every agent harness is an AI harness; a chatbot is not an agent harness.
decisions.why: The owner wanted a clear interface layer that does not count every integration as an interface, and a clear line between apps that use AI and products that are harnesses. Harness takes its industry meaning (workspace decision G-039).

decisions.decision: Execution, evidence and governance get machine-checkable records, so a venture can run end to end. A handoff is JSON at <venture>/execution/handoffs/<id>.json (handoff.schema.json) beside its Markdown brief: role, decision classes, done-criteria (conformance, self-proof, review), status, attempts, run cap, PR, evidence, escalations and lesson. Evidence is the append-only result of one run at <venture>/evidence/results/<id>.json (evidence.schema.json); eval suites follow eval-suite.schema.json. Decision rights follow decision-rights.schema.json; a venture's file tightens the template and may loosen a class only by naming a decision. schema/run-handoff.mjs runs a handoff's criteria and writes evidence; schema/check-execution.mjs holds handoffs to their role's classes, EE-006's conformance and self-proof, attempts, and passing evidence before done. Layer locations are relative to the venture folder; venture members may be agents; business models use schema/vocab/business-models.json; a product may list several markets with one primary; the Product Anatomy runner needs a revenue score of 2 for a revenue engine and counts a standalone part of the flagship kit as a wedge.
decisions.why: The first venture run (docs/design/FIRST_VENTURE_RUN_2026-10-27.md) stopped at Purpose: handoffs, evals and decision rights were prose or unchecked JSON, so the system could not run a venture end to end or settle its genus.

decisions.decision: The ecosystem has no single master schema; it has a data model. schema/data-model.json names every record type, the layer that owns it (or system, for records every layer shares), its schema, where its records live and what each references, with the check that resolves each reference. Containment runs workspace, venture, then the venture's layer records; the method's own records (catalog, ontology, decisions, evals) sit at method level outside any venture. The venture profile is one prose record inside a venture, not the master. Each layer has a kit manifest (<layer>/kit.json, kit.schema.json; the system kit at schema/kit.json) listing its skills, the record types it owns, and those of other kits it reads and writes. Layer relationships are derived from those reads and writes by schema/check-data-model.mjs, never drawn by hand. The check fails when a JSON file has no record type, a schema governs none, a record type has no owning kit or one of another layer, or a skill belongs to no kit or two. schema/validate.py takes its file-to-schema map from the data model.
decisions.why: The owner asked how the layers relate, which skills and schemas (kits) belong to which layer, and whether a master schema, perhaps the profile, contains everything. Nothing recorded the answer, so placements had drifted (a methodology skill under knowledge, a harness hooks file under knowledge, execution and interface with no skills) without any check noticing.

decisions.decision: Execution checks a handoff before executing it: its definition of ready. schema/check-ready.mjs fails unless the brief has an Outcome and a Work section with no placeholders (TBD, TODO, template markers); every product, governing decision, input file and criterion script it names exists; it names the methodology assignment it runs under (an A-NNN, ratified) or says none; its role exists and owns every decision class it carries; no escalation is open; attempts remain; and it has conformance and self-proof criteria and reviewers other than the holder. A handoff starts as draft; check-ready --record writes ready_check and moves it to ready. check-execution refuses an in-progress handoff without ready_check. Handoffs gain assignment and inputs, which is how Operations (MAD's choice) reaches Execution.
decisions.why: The owner: a handoff that reaches execution with something missing produces ambiguity, and its execution fails. Gaps must surface as questions to the author before work starts. Running the check on the three existing handoffs found one real defect: anatomy-json-output cited its methodology assignment as a governing decision.

decisions.decision: Vault and repository are universal parts of a workspace. A workspace always has a vault, the folder of documents holding venture folders and records; it has a code folder of repositories (repo, short for repository: a version-controlled store, normally Git) once any venture builds software. venture.json gains repos; a product card gains software (true when the venture builds software for it) and repo. check-ventures fails when a software product's venture, or a parent, lists no repository. Ventures in other industries may have only a vault. Operations skills name the MAD tier they serve in their kit manifest; contract-first moves from knowledge to operations, software engineering tier, beside its catalog entry.
decisions.why: The owner's workspace already splits vault and code (docs-as-code); the method should say so for every builder, and say when a repo is needed. Contract-first is a development methodology, not knowledge.

decisions.decision: The client record becomes the account record: accounts/<id>/account.json (account.schema.json), optional, for ventures that keep records per named party. Each account has a relationship: client, customer, user, member, partner or other. Who a product serves in general stays its market, which gains the same relationship (plus audience). 'client' is retired as a record name and kept as one relationship value.
decisions.why: The owner: clients are not universal; many ventures have customers, users or an audience instead. The record came from a services example. Account is the CRM-standard name for any named party; customer would sit badly over users and audiences who do not pay.

decisions.decision: The governance layer owns ownership and control. A venture's governance folder may hold ownership.json (the cap table: share classes with votes, price, liquidation terms and investor rights; holders; grants with vesting; SAFEs and notes), board.json (at most one formal board and any advisory boards: seats, who appoints them, reserved matters), founder-agreement.json with prose beside it, and exit.json (exit paths and sale values to model). Payouts are computed by schema/payouts.mjs, never typed. schema/check-governance.mjs requires a cap table and a formal board with venture-capital funding, a cap table with angel funding, and a founder agreement listing exactly the founder holders once two or more share ownership; it checks grants, classes, vesting, S-corporation single class, seats against appointing holders' board-seat rights, and that payouts add up. Five skills: cofounder-structure, board-design (formal and advisory, advisors), equity-and-share-classes, financing-and-investor-rights, exit-planning. A new decision class, ownership-or-control, is founder-owned at escalate: agents prepare options and documents and never decide. MAD's governance tier keeps governing one project; it should read who decides and funding from these records rather than ask again (to settle with the tier's name).
decisions.why: The owner: a founder needs tools for whether and how to have cofounders, boards and their powers, share types, advisors, investor rights and exits, and nothing in the system covered ownership and control. It is about the venture, not one system, so it belongs to the layer, not MAD's tier. Comparison: docs/design/GOVERNANCE_LAYER_VS_TIER_2026-10-27.md.

decisions.decision: Start with the end. A venture's purpose layer holds purpose/telos.json (telos.schema.json): the end it exists to reach, its end state and horizon, measures with one primary, the owners' intended outcome (hold, acquisition, IPO and so on) and, per Succession Matrix phase, exit criteria that each serve a measure. schema/check-telos.mjs requires every criterion to trace to a measure, governance/exit.json to prefer the telos path and not rule it out, and warns when a venture past Discovery with more than a hobby ambition has none. Other layers read rather than ask: operations/skills/methodology-selection/derive-answers.mjs derives MAD's governance-tier answers (who decides, funding, agent autonomy, success measure) from the telos, ownership, board, form and decision rights, naming each source, and lists what it cannot derive. The payout script is renamed payouts.mjs and the noun liquidation waterfall is retired for preference stack, because waterfall is a delivery methodology in MAD.
decisions.why: The owner: MAD should read the layers instead of asking again; that follows from a start-with-the-end principle, a telos record in purpose, and each phase can develop its exit from it. waterfall.mjs collided with the waterfall method in MAD's delivery tier.

decisions.decision: The genus of the Everything Ecosystem is proposed as a venture development framework, in the same genus as web development frameworks, instead of operating system or operating model (left open by EE-014). The likeness is structural: conventions over configuration (one opinionated default per choice, each with references), a fixed project structure (workspace, venture folders, layers, record types in schema/data-model.json), generators (init-venture), checks run like a test suite (node test.mjs), packages that plug in (kits, by layer and tier), and inversion of control (the framework's checks and runners call on the venture's records, as a web framework calls the application's code). An operating model describes how one organization runs; a framework is reused by many builders to build their own.
decisions.why: The owner, after the first ventures ran end to end through handoffs, evidence, governance and telos: 'I would like to consider this as a venture development framework. It would put it in a close genus with web development frameworks.'

decisions.decision: Publishing is a governance matter. Each venture keeps a publication policy (governance/publication-policy.json) that lists its channels, the guidelines each follows (brand and editorial from the pillars, plus outside rules such as platform or advertising law), the checks and preview every publication passes, and who drafts and who approves by role or team. Every publication passes this gate: it runs as a handoff under public-commitment and names its channel and content; agents may draft, check and preview, and a person approves. A channel on a third-party platform (Substack, X, Facebook and others) names the platform and cites its rules; social, newsletter and blog channels say whether replies and comments are gated, delegated to named people, or not made. publish.json moves from operations to governance as the method site's channel configuration. Publisher rule R1 now refuses only files outside the repository (an absolute path, a path through .., or a link resolving outside the root); inside it, publish.json decides.
decisions.why: The owner: 'anything being published should go through a sort of gate, especially when it's being published by an AI... It also gives us a gate to be able to test what gets published before it is actually published.' Where something is published decides which guidelines it must follow, and ventures assign publishing rights to different teams. R1 was a vault-era boundary that refused 80 of 82 allowlisted files after the method moved into its own repository; the owner approved the change.

decisions.decision: Validation is a probability built from cited evidence, not a declared phase. A validation kit in the purpose layer gives each sub-score (problem first; then solution, product-market fit, pricing, go-to-market, team, operations readiness per MAD tier) its own record type, template and references, all sharing one evidence item. schema/check-validation.mjs grades every item and record high, moderate, low or very low by adapting GRADE: the kind of signal sets the start (behavior high, commitment moderate, stated intent and desk research low, opinion very low), and the wrong audience, a small sample, general answers and age lower it; a claim with no evidence is very low. The grade weighs the sub-score's Jev probability in the validation score. A layer may hold more than one kit, under <layer>/kits/<kit>/.
decisions.why: The owner: validation 'cannot be an arbitrary measure', must not be Boolean, must cite its evidence, and evidence from the wrong audience should count for less; 'a weak record would only state the problem; a strong record would also contain market research that proves the problem is there'.

decisions.decision: Working name for the system: Mentura, from mentor and Ventura: a mentor that guides a venture into its future. Files keep 'Everything Ecosystem' until the name is checked (trademark, domains) and a rename is decided.
decisions.why: The owner: 'We can go with the name Mentura for now.'

decisions.decision: The framework says what a venture needs now, what comes soon and what to hold back. schema/need-now.json gives each venture record type a prior probability per phase, raised or lowered by facts about the venture (people, founders, agents, funding, legal form, products, go-to-market path, publishing); schema/need-now.mjs lists records to suggest now (0.5 or more), coming soon (the next phase reaches 0.5), held, and held back. Jev re-scores the priors per venture once the scorer runs.
decisions.why: The owner: early on 'there's a lot that you shouldn't spend time thinking about'; Jev should determine 'the records that they need at a particular moment and the probability of when they're going to need them later', and low-probability records are not suggested until needed or asked for.

decisions.decision: The operations layer designs the team: operations/team-plan.json says which roles agents fill and which people fill, by phase, with the decision classes each holds and a named human loop for every agent task that the capability register marks can-with-review, cannot, not-allowed or unknown. Open person roles needed in the current phase are recruited now, from a brief; agents draft, search and screen, and a person makes contact and decides. The evidence layer keeps the capability register, dated and sourced, fed by new research and by our own evals; an unknown task keeps a person in the loop and becomes an eval.
decisions.why: The owner: one-shotting a venture is possible 'because of agents who can act as team members'; the operations suite is also for 'developing the agents and teammates and delegating authority', deciding what agents and teammates you need, and recruiting real humans; and 'the literature on what can and cannot be done using agents is still very new', so we must keep reading new information or produce it ourselves.

decisions.decision: The system has one route table, generated from schema/data-model.json and the kit manifests by interface/router.mjs, and three interfaces over it: a CLI (interface/cli/mentura.mjs), an MCP server (interface/mcp/server.mjs) and a local HTTP API (interface/api/server.mjs). A route is <layer>[/<kit>]/<record> with the actions read, write, check and template, or a command with run. Every write is validated against the record's schema; an agent's write to a record whose decision class escalates to a person (ownership, board, founder agreement, exit, telos, decision rights, publication policy) is held as a draft for a person to accept, and the MCP server and API always write as an agent. Adoption may be partial: a venture turns on only the layers it wants (init --layers), and a route needs only its own records. An install skill sets it up in Claude Code and Cursor.
decisions.why: The owner: turn this into an MCP, set up APIs and a CLI, with a skill for installing it into a coding agent; builders do not have to use the entire system; consider a routing system like Next.js's. Generating routes from the kits keeps the three interfaces from drifting apart, and the draft gate carries EE-022, EE-023 and EE-025 (people decide escalate classes) into every interface.

decisions.decision: Provenance is built in two ways. Explicitly: every write through the router (CLI, MCP server, HTTP API) appends one line to the venture's provenance log, <venture>/provenance.jsonl, after W3C PROV: the entity (file) written, the activity (write, draft, accept, or baseline for a record adopted as it stood), the agent (person or AI agent, with id, model, session and harness where known, and the interface), what the content was derived from (paths, URLs, decision ids) and the decision or decision class it acted under, with a hash of the content. Each line carries the previous line's hash, so schema/check-provenance.mjs fails when a line is edited, removed or reordered, and warns when a logged file has changed outside the router. Implicitly: git history covers everything written outside the router. The log is a system record, on whatever layers a venture uses; record schemas carry no provenance fields. Existing provenance stays where it is: evidence items and references cite sources with checked dates, and notes carry source and ai-model.
decisions.why: The owner asked to make sure provenance is built in, explicitly or implicitly, and chose the recommendation of a separate append-only log backed by git over a provenance block inside every record, which would add noise to every schema.

decisions.decision: Routes follow the Next.js App Router's conventions, with layers kept as route segments so a route is its record's folder path. Built: [id] item routes for collections (products, accounts, handoffs, evidence) beside their list routes; the venture as a catch-all segment, an id or a nested venture's folder path (studio/print); layout (the system, layer and kit context, skills, references, template, gate and need-now status an agent gets before acting); not-found (a missing record answers with its template, schema, skills and need-now status), loading (a waiting draft is reported on read) and error (a failed check or write answers with the kit's skills and template); views, Markdown pages for people (the page convention), and system/overview, a page of parallel slots where one failing slot does not stop the others; route groups by phase, (discovery) to (platform), which gather the routes need-now suggests in that phase without changing paths; robots, the routes a team-plan role may read and write, shown at system/robots; route aliases for renames (interface/route-aliases.json); and gates declared in the data model (decision_class on a record type), applied from the venture's decision rights instead of a list in code.
decisions.why: The owner asked to study how Next.js uses routes and all their types, chose to keep layers as segments with groups for cross-cutting slices such as phases, and asked to build every route type we did not have.

decisions.decision: File formats are chosen by the first of these that holds: a program reads or writes it, so JSON with a schema; an append-only log, so JSONL; another tool expects the name (SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md, vault notes), so .md; prose for people that is published or needs a component or live data, so MDX; prose that stays private, so .md. MDX pages must compile (site/scripts/check-mdx.mjs, run by test.mjs and CI). See EE-071.
decisions.why: The owner wants MDX preferred over Markdown and asked for a convention for when to use MDX versus JSON or other formats. Generated pages in MDX render the repository's data at build time instead of being copied, so they cannot go stale.

decisions.decision: The developer docs are a Nextra 4 site (docs theme) on the latest Next.js, in site/ of this repository rather than a separate repo, so docs and code change in one pull request and the site renders routes, nouns, kits and decisions from the repository at build time. It reads method-level records only, never an instance venture. It stays unpublished (noindex, no deploy) until the owner accepts the developer-docs channel in the venture's publication policy, drafted for that decision. zod is pinned to 4.1.12 because later 4.x releases reject the theme's optional props. See EE-071.
decisions.why: The owner chose Nextra's documentation starter for the developer docs, on the latest Next.js, and asked whether the site belongs in a separate repo; the starter kit itself pins Next.js 13 and the Pages Router, which Nextra 4 no longer supports.

decisions.decision: Mentura replaces SAD as the builder's methodology, and SAD is one of its layers (knowledge). SAD also continues as its own project (the sad-methodology repository and site), developed independently. From here on Mentura's knowledge layer is its own version of SAD: it starts from SAD v3 and its amendments as they stand in knowledge/method/, changes only by Mentura's decisions, and neither inherits from nor syncs with the separate SAD project. A change worth sharing is ported by hand, in either direction.
decisions.why: The owner said the system being built replaces the SAD methodology and that SAD is a layer within Mentura, and chose to keep the two as separate projects, with the SAD inside Mentura being its own version from here on.

decisions.decision: SAD is removed from Mentura. The knowledge layer is the memory layer: where every record is stored and found (route, schema, provenance), holding the decision log, venture profile, design documents and references. Every other layer defines the records it writes to memory and their conventions; operations (MAD) is the one layer that is a method rather than record conventions. Storage is not fixed: files today, a database possible later. The SAD method documents, systems, references, artifacts, templates and seventeen SAD skills are deleted (git keeps them); the layer keeps two skills, find-reference and industry-awareness. SAD's surviving rules become checks and skills in the layers that need them. SAD continues as its own separate project.
decisions.why: The owner judged that with routing, schemas and provenance in place SAD was no longer necessary: a database or a file system could be the knowledge layer, and the other layers' conventions are what get written to it. He asked to run the five-step algorithm on the knowledge layer and start nearly from scratch.

decisions.decision: The knowledge layer federates rather than copies. Records stay in the sources a venture already uses, and the venture decides which record type lives where in an optional knowledge/sources.json; without one, everything stays in the venture folder. Each source is reached through a connector with one contract (list, read, version, search, write where allowed), registered as an integration with a connector in knowledge/tooling/integrations.json. A version is the git blob SHA-1 of the content in every source, and a read says its source, version and, for GitHub, a permalink at the commit, so provenance can cite it. The router reads and writes every record through the connector for its source, so its call is asynchronous. A catalog indexes every item's address, version, route, title and words, and keeps no content. The first two connectors are the file system (folders and git repositories, writing in place) and GitHub (REST over fetch, writing by draft pull request, which a person accepts by merging). Every connector passes one eval suite (knowledge/connectors/eval.mjs), run offline against a fake of the GitHub API and live when a repository and token are given.
decisions.why: The owner asked to think from first principles about a knowledge layer that may span repositories, wikis, Slack, Notion and Salesforce, held that ventures organise their own knowledge so Mentura should not be too opinionated, and asked to start with two connections plus evals that prove they work. He chose writes by pull request for GitHub (2026-10-28), matching the rule that a person merges.

decisions.decision: Operations in Mentura is business operations: the team plan and hiring, handing work to people and agents, and the tools each business function uses (marketing, sales, research; treg is a candidate integration). Every venture has it, with or without a repository. Execution folds into operations: a handoff is how operational work is assigned, so handoffs move to <venture>/operations/handoffs/ and the execution/handoff route aliases to operations/handoff. Mentura has six layers: purpose, knowledge, operations, evidence, governance, interface. MAD, the method for building software or hardware (its catalog, methodology selection, assignments, recommendations, answers and the method-site publisher), leaves Mentura to be its own product that reads Mentura's records when a venture has a repository; git keeps what was removed. MAD's governance and delivery questions (is it worth doing, who decides, how work is planned and handed over) are general business questions, to be re-homed in Mentura's governance and operations layers. Evidence stays: its results and evals are records.
decisions.why: The owner asked whether everything except MAD and evidence is knowledge, and ran the five-step algorithm on it. A venture with no repository still needs operations for marketing, hiring and the like, and two of MAD's tiers are about the business rather than the build; so only the build side of operations is a separate product.

decisions.decision: Validation evidence comes from how audiences receive a product, irrespective of the repository: website and product analytics (Vercel, Cloudflare, Netlify, Google Analytics, PostHog, Amplitude, or whoever the venture deploys with or keeps its analytics in) and customer research (Listen Labs) are evidence-layer integrations and sources of truth for validation, beside revenue (Stripe). Business operations reads these, not code quality or build speed, which are MAD's. Jev (TypeSafe AI) routes each venture to the connectors that fit its use cases, and also scores validation sub-scores. All are candidates until a connector is built and evaluated against the contract (EE-037). Under EE-041 this is platform: the entries stay as candidate data in the integrations lists, and any connector to these services, and Jev's routing, lives in platform/.
decisions.why: The owner, 2026-10-28: business operations doesn't need to know how good the code is or how fast it is built; it needs to know how different audiences are receiving it. Separating MAD from Mentura (EE-038) lets Mentura focus on sources of truth that are irrespective of the repo.

decisions.decision: MAD's governance and delivery questions that are about the business, not the build, are answered by Mentura records, and MAD reads them there (EE-038). Most already had a home: problem validated and evidence method (purpose/validation), customer reachable (validation-go-to-market), who decides (ownership, board), funding (venture form.funding), success measure and goal setting (telos measures and exit criteria), teams to align and agent share (team plan), agent autonomy and gates (decision rights, handoffs), unattended runs (handoff run caps), source of truth (knowledge/sources.json). The rest get homes: telos.steering (go decision, review cadence, change of direction), venture.regulation (regulatory exposure), and three decision classes in the template (continue-or-stop, change-direction, set-priorities). Questions about how software is built (requirements stability, sequencing, verification timing, cost of failure, flow, size and the like) stay MAD's. Map: docs/design/MAD_QUESTIONS_REHOMED_2026-10-28.md.
decisions.why: EE-038 left MAD's business questions without a home in Mentura; the owner asked to re-home them (2026-10-28) so that every venture, with or without a repository, can answer them.

decisions.decision: Mentura has two sides, as Next.js and Vercel do. The framework is the conventions: anything that works offline, with no account and without naming a vendor (record schemas and the data model, kits, the router with its CLI, MCP server and local API, routes, provenance, checks, need-now priors, validation scoring, init-venture and templates, the connector contract and the filesystem connector, the docs). The platform hosts, connects and integrates: connectors that reach a vendor (GitHub first), the connect flow, integrations that call outside services (analytics, Listen Labs, Jev routing, treg), a hosted catalog and search, the operator console and a template gallery. Both stay in this repository (Torian's choice, 2026-10-28) with a hard boundary: platform code lives in platform/, nothing outside it imports from it, and a framework connector reaches no network and names no credentials; schema/check-boundary.mjs enforces this. The framework may load a platform connector by the module path the registry names, as Next.js loads a deployment adapter. Each layer's tooling/integrations.json stays framework while its entries are data only. The framework is the open core and the platform is what is sold. Which side carries the name Mentura is open.

The knowledge layer's source map becomes a source-of-truth matrix, after master data management (DAMA-DMBOK's reference and master data). Each rule is one cell: for a record type, an attribute ('*' for the whole record) and a context (phase, product, account, actor), it names the system of record and the owner, with optional survivorship rules when the same record also lives elsewhere. Rules are written for a fast (System 1) model such as Jev to read: flat, every field present, '*' for any. Resolution is deterministic and needs no model: the matching rule with the most narrowing fields wins, and two rules that can hold at once at the same specificity are an error (schema/check-sources.mjs, knowledge/connectors/resolve.mjs). The router resolves each read and write by its context. `records` stays as shorthand for rules that match anything. A where-used list (knowledge/where-used.json) names, for each fact kept once in its system of record, every place that repeats it, each live or frozen and delivered by an agent, a person or the platform; schema/check-where-used.mjs reports drift offline. This is registry-style MDM and is framework; delivering a change into vendors' systems (coexistence or centralized style), running survivorship across vendors and a managed store for a whole venture are platform (EE-041). An attribute mastered elsewhere is read from and written to its own system of record, kept at the record's path as a JSON object holding only that attribute, and left out of the record's own file, so it lives in one place (a gated agent write stays whole as a draft until a person accepts it); a vendor's connector maps that onto its system, which is the platform's. Renaming the layer to 'source of truth' is open.

Names (Torian): the platform is Mentura (EE-027), and the framework is Naive, the conventions side of EE-041. Naive replaces the earlier working name Memento, which collides with Memento Database. Files keep 'Everything Ecosystem' until a rename is decided; a trademark check on both names is pending.

A marketing website is business operations (the marketing function), not engineering: it belongs to neither MAD nor a software engineering suite. Many tools build websites; Mentura is opinionated: the site's source lives in GitHub, it deploys from a host the venture chooses with Vercel the default, and it starts from a Vercel template (operations/tooling/integrations.json). These defaults are framework data; deploying through a host's API is platform (EE-041). Its pages are MDX, edited by agents, with skills that define how the site is designed; no CMS by default, since a CMS is an editor for people and Mentura is opinionated towards AI-native building, in business operations too (Torian, 2026-10-28). An MDX page may read facts from their system of record at build (a price component), so it never drifts (EE-042). Research on MDX for marketing pages is pending.

Mentura's ideal customer profile: solo entrepreneurs, low- to no-code founders and small teams in the early phases of business development (Discovery and Validation, not yet scaling), who build AI-native with agents as their editors and team members. Defaults are chosen for them first: agents over people as editors, files and skills over hosted tools, one opinionated choice per decision. A choice that only pays off at scale waits until need-now raises it (EE-028).

A venture's tagline is a brand record: the enduring short line a brand keeps across campaigns, such as Burger King's 'Have it your way'. It sits in venture.json under brand.tagline, owned by the brand pillar's verbal identity, and like any attribute it can have its system of record elsewhere through the source-of-truth matrix (EE-042). 'Tagline' is used rather than 'slogan' because in marketing practice a slogan often belongs to one campaign (Keller and Swaminathan's brand elements call both slogans; governance/references/references.json); a campaign's slogan belongs to the campaign, a Brand-pillar product. Mentura's tagline: 'A mentor for your journey' (Torian).

A venture is organized by department in two layers. The departments are the top-level categories of APQC's Process Classification Framework under short ids (operations/departments.json), each tagged with its place in Porter's value chain: primary (products, marketing and sales, supply chain, service delivery, customer service) or support (strategy, human capital, IT, finance, assets, legal risk and compliance, external relationships, business capabilities). A department's governance side (charter, policies, decision rights) sits in governance/departments/<id>/, and its work, assets and tools in operations/departments/<id>/. HR is a support activity, not governance: governance is who decides and oversees, and every department has a governance side (Torian asked, 2026-10-28). Each department folder holds a department.json tag, and the tag, not the folder, says what it is: grouping departments under primary/ and support/ folders is optional and for looking at only (Torian). Pillars stay: they group the work by part of the company, departments by function. Checked by schema/check-departments.mjs.

A venture holds only what it uses, when it needs it (Torian). Schemas stay in the framework and are never copied into a venture; a venture imports what it uses by listing it in venture.json, the way package.json lists dependencies, and gets folders only for what it lists. Need-now (EE-028) says when a part becomes needed, and the agent suggests it then; `mentura add <department> --venture <id>` (schema/add-department.mjs) imports a department. Departments are the first part imported this way; layers already start off until needed (EE-012), and the same rule applies across the system. The list is data an agent edits rather than imports in code, which suits the ICP (EE-045); a typed config file can come later for developers. Torian's line 'What you need, when you need it' is proposed as Naive's tagline, Mentura keeping 'A mentor for your journey' (EE-046).

The validation kit starts lean, with the problem only, and gives no single score and never a 'not viable' verdict. The problem splits into four assumptions (exists, segment, hurts, why-now); each evidence item names the one it bears on and is labelled demonstrated, inferred, assumed, unknown or contradicted. Only first-hand behavior or commitment from five or more people in the target segment, under 18 months old, demonstrates; anything reported (a vendor's customer count, desk research) infers; competitors with paying customers infer the problem and never count against it; contradicted needs evidence against from the segment at least as strong as the best for. The labels say which commitment the evidence supports, on a ladder after The Founders Bay's 'evidence strong enough for the commitment it unlocks': explore, prototype (exists and hurts inferred), charge (segment and hurts demonstrated) and raise, with the cheapest test for each blocking assumption. Before it runs, the assessment lists what is missing from the record and what running as is would mean, and asks the person to fill it in or run as is; the router, CLI, MCP server, API and skill all do this, and the caller passes as_is only after the person chose it (Torian). The behaviors are written first as Gherkin scenarios (purpose/kits/validation/features/problem-assessment.feature) and run as tests by schema/bdd.mjs. The problem record holds a root problem in statement and the forms it takes (forms[]), each assessed from its own evidence (evidence form), which also counts for the root; a form can be dropped. The problem record is gated like the telos (strategy-or-constitution): an agent's write is a draft the founder accepts. The single validation score (EE-026) is held.
decisions.why: Torian, 2026-10-28, after running Mentura and Naive through the kit: the run showed more issues in the suite than in the venture; competitors in a market can indicate a real need; one encoded framework is too constraining and risks telling a founder a great idea is not viable. He asked to start very lean with the problem, guard against false negatives and false positives, use behavior-driven development to say what the suite must do, and have it ask before running when the schema is incomplete.

decisions.decision: Guiding statements: the records a founder keeps in front of them every day, framed by the Five Ws and How plus whether (Stage-Gate's go/kill decision), with brand beside them. purpose/guiding-statements.json maps each question to attributes of existing records: why (problem, vision), what (mission as the core promise, products), who (the ICP, promised to), how (competence, business models), when (phase, exit criteria), where (markets, channels), whether (must-not; go/kill criteria, planned) and brand (tagline). A new ICP record (purpose/icp.json) holds who the venture serves, one primary profile, linked to the problem's forms. schema/guiding.mjs (route purpose/guiding) reports each statement as confirmed, agent, draft, missing or planned from the provenance log: a statement an agent wrote is not the founder's until a person writes, accepts or confirms it. Confirming and accepting are a danger zone: `mentura confirm <statement>` and `mentura accept` of a record holding a guiding statement show the change and need the person to type its name (--confirm <name> off a terminal); provenance gains a confirm activity. The ICP is gated like the telos. Always-visible presence, a daily review and recall practice, delegation unlocked by confirmed statements, and the whether forecast (environmental scanning, a calibrated probability per go/kill criterion) follow; monitoring is platform.
decisions.why: Torian, 2026-10-28: some records must always be in front of the founder until they are muscle memory (problem, vision, mission, taglines, ICP, the current phase); they should be hard to write and change, like a danger zone, and completing them should unlock delegation. He chose the frame: what, who, why, how, when and whether, and wants whether to become a constantly monitoring forecast ('likeliness of rain').

decisions.decision: The records EE-051 called guiding statements are the venture's strategic foundation; each one is a foundation statement. Files and routes follow: purpose/strategic-foundation.json, schema/foundation.mjs, route purpose/foundation. 'Guiding statement' is retired as a noun. The whether question is not settled: go/kill is too narrow, and the go/kill record built after EE-051 is held, not merged. The open question (Torian, 2026-10-28) is whether the whether review should answer persevere, pivot, pause or stop (Ries's pivot or persevere; Stage-Gate's go, kill, hold and recycle). He took up that question; he has not agreed to a four-answer review or to any design for it.
decisions.why: Torian chose 'Strategic foundation' on a decision card (standards first, EE-014). On go/kill: 'a lot of times the answer may not be kill, it may be pivot', and many great founders persevered where a go/kill framework would have said kill.

decisions.decision: The developer docs move from Nextra to Fumadocs in site/. This supersedes the Nextra sentence of EE-034. This venture's marketing pages live in the same app. They may read only the facts named in the Naive docs handoff (the problem statement and the segment), written by site/scripts/venture-facts.mjs to site/generated/venture-facts.json. site/scripts/data.mjs still reads no instance venture. This supersedes EE-034's "never an instance venture" for that one file only. test.mjs and the site CI job run npm run check:content instead of site/scripts/check-mdx.mjs. This supersedes that clause of EE-033. The zod 4.1.12 pin may be removed once Nextra is gone and the build passes. This supersedes the zod sentence of EE-034. These marketing pages are added to the existing docs app and do not start from a Vercel template. The template stays the default for a later standalone marketing site. This supersedes that clause of proposed EE-044.
decisions.why: The handoff naive-docs-and-marketing-site carries this migration, and Torian accepts it by merging. Draft PR #19 uses EE-053 through EE-070. EE-049 stays unused. The next free id on main and the open pull requests is EE-071.
